questions.question_text: In a nut mix the ratio of peanuts to walnuts to cashews is $4:3:2$. There are $18$ cashews. How many walnuts are there?

options.why: Found the peanuts, $4$ parts, instead of the walnuts.
Treated the $18$ cashews as $3$ parts, giving $6$ per part, then took $2$ parts.
Multiplied $18$ by $3$, using the walnut part count as a scale factor instead of dividing first.

questions.solution_text:
$2\text{ parts}=18$
$1\text{ part}=9$
$3\text{ parts}=27$
There are $27$ walnuts.

questions.question_text: A jeweller makes an alloy by melting $12$ g of gold with $20$ g of silver. To make more of exactly the same alloy she uses $35$ g of silver. How much gold does she need?

options.why: Added the extra $15$ g of silver to the $12$ g of gold, treating the ratio as a fixed difference.
Multiplied $12$ g by $5$, using the silver's part count as the scale factor without dividing first.
Used the same mass of gold as silver, ignoring the $3:5$ ratio altogether.

questions.solution_text:
$12:20$
$=3:5$
$5\text{ parts}=35\text{ g}$
$1\text{ part}=7\text{ g}$
$3\text{ parts}=21\text{ g}$
She needs $21$ g of gold.

questions.question_text: A rectangle has its width and length in the ratio $2:7$. The length is $35$ cm. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?

options.why: Added the width and the length but did not double to find the perimeter.
Used the value of one part, $5$ cm, as the width instead of the $2$ parts required.
Doubled the length only, leaving the two widths out of the perimeter.

questions.solution_text:
$7\text{ parts}=35\text{ cm}$
$1\text{ part}=5\text{ cm}$
$2\text{ parts}=10\text{ cm}$
$P=2\times(10+35)$
$=90\text{ cm}$

questions.question_text: On a library shelf the ratio of fiction to non-fiction books is $9:4$. There are $20$ non-fiction books. Some fiction books are then borrowed and the ratio becomes $3:2$, with the number of non-fiction books unchanged. How many fiction books were borrowed?

options.why: Gave the new number of fiction books instead of how many were borrowed.
Gave the original number of fiction books instead of how many were borrowed.
Gave the value of one part of the original ratio instead of the actual drop in books.

questions.solution_text:
$4\text{ parts}=20$
$1\text{ part}=5$
$9\text{ parts}=45\text{ fiction books at first}$
$2\text{ new parts}=20$
$1\text{ new part}=10$
$3\text{ new parts}=30\text{ fiction books now}$
$45-30=15\text{ borrowed}$
